full_judgment:
Md. Altaf Hossain, J.—This application under section 115 of the Civil Procedure Code is directed against the judgment and order dated 27.11.81 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 182 of 1978 allowing the appeal and setting aside the order dated 29.4.78 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong in title suit No. 98 of 1977 granting plaintiff's prayer for appointment of receiver and appointing a receiver. 

 2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted the aforesaid Title Suit No. 98 of 1977 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong, for declaration of title and recovery of possession of the suit property claiming title on the basis of an auction purchase in Certificate Case Nos. 88, 89, 90, 91, and 92 I.T. of 1964-65. After filing the suit the plaintiff also filed an application under Order 40, rule I. C.P.C. for appointment of receiver on the ground, inter alia, that the defendant No. 1 who originally entered as his tenant and was subsequently continuing in permissive possession, has inducted defendant Nos. 2 to 4 as monthly tenants and is trying to encumber the suit property in various other ways and is also trying to sell out the property to a third party. The petition was opposed by the defendant-opposite party No. 1 who alleged that the plaintiff was his benamdar. The learned Subordinate Judge after hearing both the parties granted plaintiff's prayer for appointment of receiver and appointed one Mr. Md. Ali, advocate, as receiver. The receiver was also directed to take possession of the property from the defendant No. 1 for its proper maintenance and preservation. The defendant-opposite party preferred an appeal to the District Judge and the learned Additional District Judge who heard the appeal, after hearing both the parties, allowed the appeal by the impugned order dated 29.4.78 and set aside the order of the learned Subordinate Judge. 

 The plaintiff-petitioner has, thereupon, moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 3. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioner has taken us through the judgments of the courts below. The learned Advocate submits that the learned Subordinate Judge has granted his prayer for appointment of receiver on the finding that the plaintiff had a good prima facie case and on holding that a receiver should be appointed for the maintenance and preservation of the suit property but the learned Additional District Judge without reversing the finding of the learned Subordinate Judge had set aside his order. The learned Additional District Judge has committed an error of law apparent on the face of the record. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Additional District Judge has misconceived the provision of sub-rule (2) of rule 1 of Order 40 of the C.P.C. and erroneously held that as the defendant was admittedly in possession of the suit property there could not and should not be a receiver. 

 4. Mr. B. K. Das, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-opposite party No. 1, on the other hand, submits that the learned Additional District Judge has rightly set aside the order of the learned Subordinate Judge inasmuch as it was not just and convenient in the facts and circumstances of the case to appoint a receiver. He further submits that the learned Additional District Judge was rightly of the view that even if the apprehension of the plaintiff were true it could be a good ground for temporary injunction restraining the defendant-appellant from transferring the suit land but not a cogent ground for appointment of receiver. The learned Advocate further submits that his client undertakes not to transfer the suit land to anybody till disposal of the suit and also not to induct any other tenant in the premises or to otherwise encumber it. 

 5. Order 40, rule 1(2) provides that anything in this rule shall authorise the court to remove from the possession or custody of property any person whom any party to the suit land has not a present right so to remove. The learned Additional District Judge has, relying on this sub-rule, held that as the defendant-appellant was admittedly in possession there could not be and should not be any receiver. It is apparent that the learned Additional District Judge has misconceived the provision of sub-rule (2) of rule 1 of Order 40. It is now settled by judicial decisions that the word "person" within the meaning of the sub-rule means a person other than a party and as such does not put any bar upon the court to appoint a receiver and remove the defendant from possession. Mr. Das does not dispute this proposition of law. The reliance of the learned Additional District Judge on sub-rule (2) in refusing plaintiff's prayer for temporary injunction cannot, therefore, be said to be correct. This is, however, not to say that the possession of the defendant in the suit property is not at all a relevant matter for consideration for appointment of receiver. If it appears that removal of the defendant from possession will result in causing irreparable wrong to him the court may certainly consider it and refuse plaintiff's prayer for appointment of receiver. 

 6. The learned Additional District Judge, even though he has erroneously sought reliance on the provision of sub-rule (2) of rule 1 of Order 40 C.P.C. has also referred to the decision of Nur Mohamad vs. Jogendra Dutta reported in 28 D.L.R. 7, wherein it has been held that an order for appointment of receiver will not be made if it has effect of depriving a defendant of defector possession since that might cause irreparable wrong. The learned Additional District Judge has also observed that even if the apprehensions of the plaintiff-respondent be taken to be true, they can be very good ground for temporary injunction restraining the defendant appellant from transferring the suit land to any one during the pendency of the suit, but they are never cogent grounds for appointment of receiver under Order 40 rule 1 C.P.C. It is, therefore evident that the learned Additional District Judge has been of the opinion that if the defendant is removed from possession he will suffer irreparable wrong and a temporary injunction is an adequate relief and it is not an appropriate case for appointment of receiver. We are unable to say that the learned Additional District Judge has made an error of law in taking this view. Furthermore, Order 40 rule 1 C.P.C. empowers the court to appoint a receiver only when it appears to the court to be just and convenient. The order of the learned Subordinate Judge does not show that it appeared to him to be just and convenient that a receiver should be appointed. We are of the opinion that in every case where a receiver is appointed the order of the court should indicate that it appears to it to be just and convenient that a receiver should be appointed. This should not be left for being inferred from other observations made in the order. In the present case, the learned Subordinate Judge merely stated that the plaintiff apprehends transfer of the suit land by the defendant and has held that a receiver should be appointed. We are unable to hold that this is a cogent ground for appointment of a receiver particularly when, in the instant case, the learned Advocate for the opposite party has given undertaking on behalf of his client that the opposite party will not transfer the suit property to anybody and will not induct any other tenant and otherwise encumber the same.
